resources.string: Shown while ArrowLoop is able to sync in the background.
Ready to sync, and able to keep going while the screen is off.
The engine did not answer within thirty seconds. Its own log ends like this:\n\n%1$s
ArrowLoop needs access to your files

To sync a folder, ArrowLoop has to be able to read and write it. Android grants that on its own settings page, which the button below opens.\n\nWithout it, ArrowLoop can still run, but only inside its own private folder: your photos, your downloads and your documents stay out of reach.

This build of Android has no way to grant an app access to your files without also giving up modification times, which a two-way sync cannot work without. ArrowLoop will run, but only inside its own private folder. Android 11 and later can grant the access.
This phone has no page for that permission.
